A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all pages, including Appendices A–D, support comparison. V2 visually obscures part of Table 2, but the underlying values remain recoverable through text extraction.

before.justification: V1 reports original FineWeb and CodeParrot training results, downstream benchmark evaluations, and tokenization analyses, including the appendix downsampling-rate experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds BPE-guidance comparisons, a boundary-window ablation, and convergence and downsampling-rate measurements.

M1.justification: The U-Net architecture, score-function objective, early-exit rewards, discounting, batch centering, and rate-targeting loss are retained. The new w=1 experiment varies an existing hyperparameter; the exploratory variable-target training discussion specifies no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb, CodeParrot, PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, and LAMBADA. Added comparisons and analyses remain within this coverage. References to time-series research and potential multilingual benefits do not introduce evaluated tasks or populations.

E2.justification: V2 adds BPE guidance to Table 1 alongside the retained Uniform, Dynamic (Nawrot et al.), and H-Net (Hwang et al.) comparators. This is one additional baseline within the existing natural-language evaluation; the CodeParrot comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces zero-shot accuracy on all four downstream benchmarks with bits-per-byte assigned to the correct continuation, substantially changing the evaluation criterion. V2 also introduces the w=1 configuration and a BPE-guidance protocol with shifted boundary indicators. The FineWeb metric and existing Table 2 training settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds the w=1 ablation, boundary-policy convergence analysis in Figure 13, and inference-compute checks using Table 3's downsampling rates. It also adds CodeParrot examples in B.4–B.5 and briefly reports less effective variable-target training. The existing fixed-rate sweep in B.6 is retained.

E5.justification: V1's Table 1 contains point estimates only; v2 adds standard errors throughout, including for the unchanged FineWeb means. Neither version specifies run counts, seeds, or the standard-error calculation, so additional repeated runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: The four downstream accuracy columns are replaced by likelihood results, rather than updated under the same metric. Table 1 adds BPE-guidance and w=1 results, including FineWeb values of 1.299 and 1.280 bits-per-byte. The original four FineWeb means and both training-loss plots remain unchanged. V2 additionally reports convergence, achieved downsampling rates, and exploratory variable-target findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 2 and the derivation in Appendix A.1 are retained, with equation splitting and renumbering. Revised explanations of discreteness and architectural scope introduce no new formal result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and central conclusion retain the claims that reinforcement-learning variance reduction enables semantic boundary learning, improves over straight-through estimators at roughly the 100M-parameter scale, and supports different downsampling rates. The listed main contributions are not redefined.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the hardware-based architectural necessity argument with an explicit single-stage scope. It adds interpretations of BPE parity, the sufficiency of w=1, noisy downstream accuracy, and inference-compute differences. The expanded conclusion identifies unresolved aspect-ratio scaling and limitations of variable-target training.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-release statement and repository address. Appendix D.1 documents training the BPE tokenizer on FineWeb with a 200k vocabulary, placing boundaries at token-final bytes, and shifting the indicators, with an example. Existing architecture details and Table 2 hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wu et al. (2026) as independent concurrent work on reinforcement-learning tokenization and Beyer et al. (2023) in the variable-target discussion, while removing Yuan et al. (2025). The byte-level scaling survey moves from Appendix C.1 to Section 3.1 without a substantial change in its positioning.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the architectural motivation and experimental discussion, expands the conclusion, and adds impact and acknowledgement sections. It incorporates Appendix C.1 into related work and moves references after the appendices. Most introductory and methodological prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 converts the document to two columns, splits and recolors v1's Figure 2 into Figures 2 and 5, and moves the unchanged Figure 10 loss plots into the main text as Figures 3 and 4. It expands Table 1 and adds Figure 13 and Table 3. Appendix reflow separates headings from figures, and Figure 13 obscures Table 2's 20–40M column.

improvement.justification: The new BPE comparison, window ablation, convergence and compute checks, and code-access information make the empirical case and documentation more informative. The gain is limited by removal of direct task-accuracy results, unspecified standard-error estimation, and layout defects that obscure part of the hyperparameter table. These tradeoffs support a modest overall improvement.
